classification.difficultyReason: Derive a general truncated-pyramid formula using similarity and subtraction, then compare volumes.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Use the method of question 6 to show that the volume of a truncated square pyramid with height $h$ and square base and square top of side lengths $x$ and $y$, respectively, is given by $\frac{1}{3}h(x^2+y^2+xy)$. (A truncated pyramid is formed in a similar way to a frustum.)

answer.short:
$V=\frac{1}{3}h(x^2+y^2+xy)$.

Use similar triangles to relate the heights, then subtract the smaller pyramid from the whole pyramid.
answer.worked:
Let $H$ be the height of the whole pyramid. The removed pyramid has height $H-h$. Corresponding lengths in similar triangles give
$$\begin{align*}\frac{H-h}{H}&=\frac{y}{x}\\xH-xh&=yH\\H(x-y)&=xh\\H&=\frac{xh}{x-y}.\end{align*}$$
Subtract the volume of the removed pyramid:
$$\begin{align*}V&=\frac{1}{3}x^2H-\frac{1}{3}y^2(H-h)\\V&=\frac{1}{3}\left[H(x^2-y^2)+y^2h\right]\\V&=\frac{1}{3}\left[\frac{xh}{x-y}(x-y)(x+y)+y^2h\right]\\V&=\frac{1}{3}h\left[x(x+y)+y^2\right]\\V&=\frac{1}{3}h(x^2+y^2+xy).\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: If the top square has a side length that is half that of the bottom square, what is the ratio of the volume of the truncated pyramid to that of the whole pyramid?

answer.short:
$7:8$.

The removed pyramid has half the corresponding lengths, so its volume is one-eighth of the whole pyramid.
answer.worked:
The removed pyramid and the whole pyramid are similar, with corresponding side-length ratio $1:2$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{V_{\text{removed}}}{V_{\text{whole}}}&=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3\\\frac{V_{\text{removed}}}{V_{\text{whole}}}&=\frac{1}{8}\\\frac{V_{\text{truncated}}}{V_{\text{whole}}}&=1-\frac{1}{8}\\\frac{V_{\text{truncated}}}{V_{\text{whole}}}&=\frac{7}{8}.\end{align*}$$
The required ratio is $7:8$.
